messages:
Alex: Hey, AcmePayments filed an escalation: SSE streams drop after ~10-20s when their consumer is slow. They see partial JSON objects and the client reports socket write errors. Attaching their minimal repro and our logs below.

Jordan: Thx. Do we have their repro code? Also which region/cluster is affected?

Alex: They repro with both curl and a simple Python requests stream. Example they sent: 

```
# curl repro
curl -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=llama-xxl\" | while read line; do sleep 0.15; echo "$line"; done
```

They say it reliably disconnects after 12-18s.

Maria: Share runtime/gateway logs around that time. We need gw/runtime and nginx or envoy traces.

Alex: Pasted logs (redacted ids):

```
[2026-03-08T08:41:22Z] stream_id=stream-77 INFO queued 8KB to write
[2026-03-08T08:41:23Z] stream_id=stream-77 WARN socket write blocked, queue_len=65536
[2026-03-08T08:41:24Z] stream_id=stream-77 ERROR write failure: EPIPE (broken pipe)
[2026-03-08T08:41:24Z] stream_id=stream-77 INFO connection closed by peer (code=1006)
```

Alex: Browser console (customer) shows ERR_HTTP2_STREAM_ERROR in some cases. Node h2 client shows ECONNRESET.

Jordan: Sounds like classic slow-consumer/backpressure: kernel send buffer fills, our write path blocks, and either our runtime gives up or the proxy resets the upstream. Questions: 1) Are we hitting a write retry ceiling in runtime? 2) Does the gateway have a short upstream timeout that triggers resets when writes block? 3) Are HTTP/2 WINDOW_UPDATE frames being propagated properly?

Maria: I pulled metrics from the host serving that customer in prod-us-1: tcp_sndbuf consumption spikes and the socket send queue grows to >1MB before the EPIPE. No OOM. The gateway (envoy) hasn't logged upstream 504s but did show a stream reset.

eng-oncall-bot: Ticket INC-2026-198 opened and assigned to eng-runtime + eng-sre: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-198

Customer-ops (Acme): We confirmed this pattern across our browser and a server-side Node client. If we process faster (sleep 0.01), stream is stable. With sleep 0.15 it fails. We're worried about duplicate charges when the client reconnects and the model replays tokens.

Billing: We're aware. Please collect trace ids/time windows; we'll consider provisional credits for verified duplicates while root cause is investigated. Also we should throttle token billing on reconnect storms to avoid overcharging.

Jordan: Quick triage steps we recommend to Acme: 1) Reduce client-side processing latency where possible. 2) Use our SDK streaming helpers which apply backpressure signals (writableStream.ready) rather than naive line-by-line drains. 3) Add idempotency/session keys so retries don't re-bill for previously accepted tokens.

Alex: Provided repro script for their security/audit team to run:

```
# repro_py.py
import requests, time
url = 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?token=REDACTED'
r = requests.get(url, stream=True)
for chunk in r.iter_content(chunk_size=512):
    print('recv', len(chunk))
    time.sleep(0.15)  # slow consumer
```

Maria: On our side configuration checks: envoy proxy send/receive window, runtime write retry/backoff settings, per-connection max-queued-bytes, and kernel tcp_wmem/tcp_rmem. Also check HTTP/2 flow control: if the client stops sending WINDOW_UPDATE we may be blocked waiting for it.

eng-sre: I'm seeing no recent global config changes, but one node had custom iptables tuning. I'll compare send buffer sizes across the fleet.

Jordan (eng-runtime): Runtime current behavior: non-blocking writes -> on EAGAIN we retry N times with small backoff, then record write_failed and close connection. N is currently 5. Also our chunker writes up to 32KB frames. Hypothesis: large frames + slow consumer -> kernel buffer full -> repeated EAGAIN -> hit retry cap -> abort.

Jordan: Plan for code changes: 1) reduce default SSE chunk max to 4KB, 2) increase write retry attempts and make retry window configurable per-tenant, 3) add a write_retries and slow_consumer metric and a debug log with exact retry counts and reason for close. I'll open a PR for 1 & 2 behind a runtime config flag.

Alex: Customer asked if we can toggle a tenant-level mitigation now (smaller chunk size) while we patch. For hosted customers we can add a routing-layer override. Can eng-sre do a quick config flip per-tenant?

eng-sre: We have a routing rule override service; we can gate a small-chunk transform at the gateway for that tenant for a few hours. Will coordinatesafe rollout.

Billing: Please make sure we get the customers time ranges for suspected duplicate charges; billing will prepare a credit proposal.

Maria: Also watch for HTTP/2 specific issues: some clients (browsers) use small window sizes; if the gateway isn't forwarding WINDOW_UPDATE, upstream will stall. I'll add an h2 flow-control traceable metric and correlate with the socket send-queue growth.

Customer-ops (Acme): We tested with the SDK and the issue looks less frequent; native fetch/eventsource still hits it. We'll try the suggested per-tenant toggle and report back.

Action items (summary):
- eng-runtime (Jordan): implement configurable write retries, reduce default chunk size to 4KB, add write_retries and slow_consumer metrics.
- eng-sre (Maria): audit gateway h2 flow-control behavior and apply per-tenant chunk-transform toggle for Acme.
- support (Alex): provide the repro scripts, collect trace ids, and coordinate with customer & billing.
- billing (Billing): prepare provisional credit path for verified duplicate-charge incidents.

eng-oncall-bot: INC-2026-198 updated: labels: sse, slow-consumer, billing-impact; watchers: eng-runtime, eng-sre, support

Alex: Thanks all. Customer confirmed the gateway toggle stabilized their stream for 30+ minutes. They will keep testing and we will follow up when Jordan has a runtime patch. Ping me for logs/trace ids and Ill attach them to the ticket.
